annotations.text:
WHY THIS EXISTS (28 OCTOBER 2026)

The front page (design/site/, D, built) puts a picture of the wall beside a picture of a phone, to say one house, every screen. Looking at it live, the first note was that the two look like two different apps, and that the page would be better light than dark.

Both are true of the pictures rather than of the panel. The wall picture is 7:40 in the evening and always dark. The phone picture follows the visitor's setting, so a visitor in light mode gets a phone at 1 in the afternoon beside a wall at night. And even when the two agree on the hour, the wall shows its Your evening cards while the phone shows its list of what's on: not one card in common.

The panel already has what the page needs. The wall has a Light look (design/appearance/, B, 7 October), and a room looks the same on both screens.

Only the top of the page changes here. The rest of D stays as built.

TODAY: TWO MOMENTS, TWO LAYOUTS, AND A WARNING

A light visitor, the usual case on a computer by day, gets a light page holding a dark wall at 7:40 PM next to a bright phone at 1:00 PM. A dark visitor gets the hour to match, but the wall's big cards and the phone's rows of what's on still share nothing you can point at.

The wall picture also carries Set a passcode: Anyone on your Wi-Fi can change the house right now. That's the house warning its owner, and on a front page it reads as a warning about the product. It's gone from every picture below: they're taken with a passcode set.

On a phone the wall isn't shown at all, and the phone picture is under the fold, so this is a computer's problem. The phone boards are there to show the page's light or dark, not the pairing.

A: THE SAME MOMENT

The smallest change. The page keeps following the visitor's setting, and now both pictures do too: a light visitor sees the afternoon on the wall and the phone, in Light; a dark one sees the evening on both, in Dark. The layout of the page is untouched.

GOOD: Nothing about the page moves, and the clash of day beside night is gone. It's two extra pictures in npm run site-shots and one more media query.

COSTS: It fixes the hour, not the likeness. The wall still shows its Your evening cards and the phone its list of what's on, so the two still look like different apps to anyone who looks for a moment. And the page stays dark for every dark visitor, which is about half of them.

B: THE SAME ROOM

Both pictures are the living room. The same heading, the same line under it (2 lights on, Harbor Lights, Blind open, Motion), the same TV, the same Movie, Guests, Sleep and All off. One small line under them says so: The living room, on the wall and on a phone. Light and dark follow the visitor, matched as in A.

GOOD: It's the only one of the three where the pictures prove the page's sentence. A visitor sees it's one app in a second, without reading a word. The room is also the screen people use most: it's where the house is changed, not just watched.

COSTS: The phone covers the wall's TV card, so its title is cut to "Lights". The weather and the big glass Your evening cards, the wall's most striking look, leave the top of the page; they'd go on lower down, or in the pretend house. One more picture to take, and the caption to keep true.

C: DAYLIGHT FIRST

The page is light for everyone, whatever the visitor's setting, and so are the pictures: the afternoon on both screens. One scroll down, a new section shows the same wall at 8:30, 1:00 and 7:40, all in Light, with the sky going from sand to blue to lavender, and one sentence for Dark: choose that on the wall, and each phone chooses for itself.

GOOD: It's what was asked for, and a light page reads as a home, not a TV app. The new section turns the hour-to-hour difference into a feature instead of a contradiction, and it's true of the shipped panel.

COSTS: It undoes D's "follows the visitor's setting", which Bench's page also does, so the two Elyir pages stop matching. Visitors in dark mode at night get a bright page. On its own it leaves the hero the same as A's: matched hour, different layouts. The section adds length to a page D kept short.

TO PICK

A, B or C, or something else: say it and it gets drawn.

They combine. B's room pair can sit on C's light page, with C's day strip underneath, and A's rule of matched pictures in both looks is part of B already.

Not drawn here, and worth a collection of their own: what the hub works with (the brands and kinds of things), a few lines on what it does, a short list of questions (do I need Home Assistant, does it need the internet), a preview picture for when the link is shared, and a way back to the front page from the pretend house on a phone.
